narrative:
Heppner closes September 2026 slightly behind budget: YTD revenue €210.4M (−1.9%) and YTD EBITDA €12.3M (−€0.95M). The Q3 Forecast lands FY2026 at €286.8M revenue and €17.1M EBITDA against a €292.8M / €18.1M budget.

Two things moved the year: the Q1 diesel spike (CNR index +20% by March) that the fuel surcharge recovered two months late, and three agencies — Marseille-Vitrolles, Rouen and Mulhouse — whose margin per shipment is down about 20%. On the positive side, the freight-flow optimisation model saved €0.58M of subcontracting in Q3 and now feeds the plan directly.

The FY2027 Budget is set at €303.1M (3.5% GRI, flat volume) with an EBITDA target of €18.8M (6.2%).

signals.title: Q3 forecast €286.8M — about €6M below the FY2026 budget
signals.source: SDP Q3 Forecast (9+3) vs FY2026 Budget
signals.excerpt: Full truckload and road groupage volumes are softer than budgeted. Air & sea and customs are close to plan. EBITDA lands at €17.1M, about 0.25 points of margin below budget.

signals.title: Q1 diesel spike: surcharge recovered two months late
signals.source: SDP agency margin monitor — CNR diesel index vs fuel surcharge (synthetic data)
signals.excerpt: The CNR diesel index rose about 20% between January and March 2026 (€1.52 → €1.82 per litre). The fuel surcharge followed with a two-month lag, so about €0.7M of agency contribution margin was lost in Q1.

signals.title: Three agencies behind plan on margin per shipment
signals.source: SDP agency margin monitor — FY2026 YTD (synthetic data)
signals.excerpt: Marseille-Vitrolles, Rouen and Mulhouse are together about €0.6M behind budget YTD (€0.8M for the full year): a lost key account, a higher subcontracting share after driver shortages, and cross-border surcharge lag.
